why: Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold: their PASS values follow directly from the expect lines (left padding, a space when fill is omitted, length equal to width, s unchanged when it is at or above width, and npm test exiting 0). Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition needs the regex to print `missing: none`. That regex (`^#{1,6}\s+`?name\b`, case-sensitive) only matches ATX headings that begin with the exact function name. The expect line only says README.md has "a section for every function". A real padLeft section titled "## Padding strings with padLeft", "## PadLeft", or written as a setext (underlined) heading would fail the PASS condition even though the words are met. That heading-wording rule is stricter than the expect line, so it belongs under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL.
